subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration feasibility + next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@acmeai.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration feasibility + next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and agreed next steps so nothing falls through the cracks. Appreciate you and Samir walking us through the current stack.

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency spikes on peak inference hours (p95 ~1.2s for chat flows) that are impacting conversions
- Fragmented embedding pipeline: embeddings generated in-house vs. search reranker is inconsistent across formats
- Limited ability to stream partial results to the frontend (UX needs streaming for early responses)

Goals / success metrics:
- Reduce p95 latency to <600ms for 95% of requests for the primary chat route
- Standardize embedding vector format and enable on-demand reranking with a single endpoint
- Enable streaming + structured outputs (JSON) for the new guided workflow

Product fit highlights from our side:
- SDK changes: our JS/Go SDKs support function-calling style and structured outputs; minimal client changes required (1-2 lines to enable structured output parsing)
- Function calling: Redwood supports tool/function calling to trigger downstream systems (e.g., call a product-availability API) with deterministic JSON schema enforcement
- Streaming: we can stream token deltas to the browser via chunked responses or websockets depending on your stack; sample snippets attached
- Embeddings / reranking: single API to generate embeddings + a fast reranking helper that runs locally or as a server-side call; we’ll share recommended dimension/normalization config for your existing models

Open technical questions we promised to follow up on:
1) Quantization/throughput: provide a compatibility matrix for your current model variants vs. Redwood’s quantized variants (attached)
2) KV/prefix caching: recommendation for your conversational flows (we’ll propose a policy based on average session length you shared)
3) Data residency & logging: summarize what’s available in Private vs. Hosted for compliance (we’ll loop in Security if needed)

Next steps & owners:
- Redwood: send integration compatibility matrix + sample SDK change snippets (Marissa) — by Mon 11/30
- Acme: share a representative sample of production traces (anonymized) & a tech contact for a short infra sync (Alex / Samir) — by Tue 12/1
- Schedule technical deep-dive w/ infra (Rishi + Samir) — propose Wed 12/2 10am PT (please confirm)

Attachments: redwood-integration-compat-matrix.pdf, proposed-multipage-pricing.xlsx

Thanks — happy to adjust anything I missed.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0153

- Streaming is a hard requirement for the new guided flow; happy to prioritize the infra sync.

2) For function calling, do you require a schema-first definition or do you support dynamic schemas per-request?

We can do Wed 12/2 10am PT for the infra deep-dive — Samir and I will be there.

Also looping in procurement for initial pricing doc.

Alex / Samir — attaching the compatibility matrix and a short SDK guide for the streaming + function-calling flow. Answers inline to your questions below.

Inline answers:
1) GPU compatibility: No hard blockers — A10G is supported. For quantized runtime we recommend batch sizes >=8 for throughput gains; we included per-model guidance in the matrix (attached).
2) Function calling: Redwood supports both schema-first and dynamic per-request schemas. For strict enforcement we recommend schema-first; for iterative UX flows dynamic schemas work fine but we’ll attach example validation hooks.
3) Embeddings: for 1536-d vectors we recommend cosine similarity with L2-normalization preserved; for reranking we suggest offline tiles + lightweight online reranking (we included a cost/latency tradeoff table).

What’s attached:
- redwood-integration-compat-matrix.pdf — model variants, quantization notes, recommmended batch sizes
- proposed-multipage-pricing.xlsx — starter pricing for hosted vs dedicated vs private (sensitive)
- sdk-snippets.md (link in Drive) — minimal JS/Go examples for streaming and function calling

Proposed schedule (confirmed):
- Technical deep-dive: Wed 12/2 10:00am PT (Rishi + Samir + Alex) — calendar invite sent
- Procurement touchpoint: Tue 12/8 (procurement@acmeai.com + Marissa)

Let me know if you want a short demo focused on structured outputs and reranking before the technical call.

Thanks,
Marissa
